implementerProof.how: Drove the same surface on an independent rig: base 59f6647db9d7 and head 81d5a51436ff binaries built by the tester (git archive, GOWORK=off go build ./cmd/dispatch), a fresh copy of the load-test seed database and a counting fake listener serving the implementer's 1,000-session file. Base and head GET /api/v1/agents were byte-identical for bearer and person reads (sha256 569e4bd9..., the implementer's value); 20 agents + 20 issue reads made 21 listener calls at base and 1 at head; the uncached hook made 40. The load-test CPU series and the memory figures were not re-run: the call counts and the identical bodies are the observable contract, and the load-test rule is the implementer's merge measurement, quoted on the pull request.

proof.criterion: What an agent sees does not change: same rows, fields and order for the same listener answer, at fleet size.

proof.criterion: The list is no staler than route_status (<= 5 s plus fetch), and agents and issue reads share one listener call per TTL.
proof.surface: Dispatch server binary over HTTP with a request-counting fake listener; the pi-envoy dispatch read CLI; the Agents page in Chromium
proof.command: s1-verify.sh (20 agents + 20 GET /api/v1/issues/LGA-1 interleaved, 6 s after boot); s4-cli.sh (one dispatch read, then three more); s5-burst.sh (20+20 and 50+50 concurrent after expiry); s3-browser.sh (Playwright, /agents searched for tester-probe, listener title changed mid-run, head without the test hook)
proof.observed: base 21 listener calls, head 1. One dispatch read: base 2 calls, head 1; three more: base 3, head 0. 20+20 concurrent in 3.4 s: 1 call; 50+50 in 7.5 s: 2 calls (the burst outlasted the 5 s TTL). The Agents page showed 'Tester probe one', then 'Tester probe two' 10.3 s after the listener changed, at its next 15 s poll, with 2 listener calls for the whole page run.

proof.criterion: A listener failure still answers 503 ENVOY_UNAVAILABLE (and, as accepted, a listener slower than 2 s answers 503 and a failed fetch's 503 is served up to 5 s without a new call).
proof.surface: Dispatch server binary over HTTP with a fake listener that delays, fails or garbles its answer
proof.command: $TMPDIR/infra652-test/s2-break.sh: fake delay=3 with 10 concurrent agents reads, then an issue read and an agents read inside the silence; delay=1.5 with a client that gives up at 0.5 s (curl -m 0.5); status=500; body=garbage; body=null; body=[]
proof.observed: Slow listener: 10x 503 {"code":"ENVOY_UNAVAILABLE","error":"envoy listener unavailable: GET /v1/sessions: ... context deadline exceeded"}, max 2.02 s, 1 listener call; inside the silence, the issue read answered route_status unknown in 17 ms and the agents read answered 503 in 2 ms, still 1 call. When the client gave up, the fetch ran on, and the next read was 200 with 1000 rows (1 call in total). 500 -> 503 'GET /v1/sessions returned 500'; garbage -> 503 'decode GET /v1/sessions response: ...'; null and [] -> 200 [].
proof.negativeControl: Unauthenticated read -> 401 NO_IDENTITY and wrong bearer -> 401 UNAUTHORIZED, both with 0 listener calls (an unauthenticated caller cannot start a fetch).

proof.criterion: DISPATCH_TEST_ROSTER_UNCACHED is a test-only setting refused without DISPATCH_TEST_HOOKS=1.
